{{Quote|I'm not familiar with&mdash;what are they? Vradium and ambori.”''"<br />"''Mix them together and they offer up the chemical cues that tests use to determine if a fluid contains bacta. Mix them with an inert pink fluid medium, and they look just like bacta. And so those two drugs are part of what is referred to as the Bacta Three-Way, or the Bacta Triangle Scam.|Bhindi Drayson and Jesmin Tainer|<ref name="MK">''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]''</ref>}}
'''Bacta Triangle Scam''', also known as the '''Bacta Three-Way''', was a [[Black market/Legends|black market]] scheme involving new [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]], old bacta, and a mixture of [[vradium]], [[ambori]], and an inert pink fluid medium. The scam involved secretly replacing newly delivered bacta with old bacta while filling containers intended for disposal with the chemical mixture. The mixture would pass one test confirming it as bacta, while another test would indicate that it had reached the end of its useful life and should be destroyed, allowing the stolen bacta to be sold on the black market.<ref name="MK" />

In [[44 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]'' to [[44 ABY]].</ref> [[Jesmin Tainer]] and [[Bhindi Drayson]], members of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] [[Commando/Legends|commando]] unit [[Wraith Squadron]], found casks of vradium and ambori stored at [[Glitterby Base]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vandor-3]] as part of Galactic Alliance [[Galactic Alliance Army|Army]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Stavin Thaal]]'s black market operations.<ref name="MK" />
